label: Marconi signals across the English Channel
detail: Guglielmo Marconi, who had moved to England in 1896 for funding, sends wireless signals across the Channel.

label: Marconi arrives on Cape Cod
detail: Marconi arrives in February 1901 and builds four 210 ft towers in South Wellfleet.

label: Morse 'S' heard across the Atlantic
detail: Marconi and George Kemp at Signal Hill, Newfoundland, hear the letter S sent from Poldhu, Cornwall, using a kite-borne antenna.

label: Wellfleet's transatlantic exchange
detail: A 48-word message goes from Wellfleet to England and a reply returns; Roosevelt's greeting to Edward VII is dated January 19.

label: Fessenden's documented demonstration
detail: Fessenden demonstrates his alternator transmitter at Brant Rock; about 12 W reached the antenna.

label: Claimed Christmas Eve broadcast (disputed)
detail: Fessenden's 1932 letter claims a voice-and-music broadcast; no contemporary accounts have been found.

label: Radio Act of 1912
detail: Passed after the Titanic sank; requires licenses to transmit and puts the Commerce Department in charge.

label: ARRL founded
detail: Hiram Percy Maxim and Clarence D. Tuska co-found the American Radio Relay League in Hartford, Connecticut.

label: Navy shuts Wellfleet station
detail: The Navy closes Marconi's Wellfleet station; it is dismantled in 1920.

label: WBZ licensed
detail: WBZ is licensed and first broadcasts on September 19 from the Eastern States Exposition in Springfield.

label: Court rules for Zenith's WJAZ
detail: A federal judge rules the government lacks authority to set operating requirements, leaving stations free to change frequencies.

label: Radio Act of 1927
detail: Creates the Federal Radio Commission and the 'public interest, convenience, or necessity' standard.

label: Communications Act of 1934
detail: Creates the FCC to replace the FRC and puts wire and radio under one framework.

label: First low-power unlicensed rules
detail: The FCC adopts rules for low-power devices, the ancestor of today's Part 15.

label: WBZ moves to Hull
detail: Fybush gives July 8, 1940 for the Hull dedication; Wikipedia gives July 27, 1940 for the move.

label: WBZ moves to 1030 kHz
detail: Under NARBA, WBZ moves from 990 to 1030 kHz as a clear-channel station.

label: CONELRAD created
detail: President Truman sets up CONELRAD, the first US national emergency broadcast system.

label: Cedar Street tower in Needham
detail: WBZ-TV's roughly 1,200 ft tower replaces one destroyed in 1954.

label: Needham's Cedar Street TV tower built
detail: Built for WBZ-TV; WGBH-TV, WCVB and WGBX joined later.

label: Emergency Broadcast System
detail: The Emergency Broadcast System replaces CONELRAD under President Kennedy.

label: WGBH-TV moves its transmitter to Needham
detail: WGBH-TV's signal is rated at 362.7 m (1,190 ft) above average terrain.

label: BAPERN begins
detail: The Greater Boston Police Council starts building a shared police mutual aid radio network.

label: ALOHAnet
detail: ALOHAnet links the Hawaiian Islands by UHF packet radio, an ancestor of Wi-Fi.

label: Logan Runway 14/32 first proposed
detail: The runway would not open for another 33 years.

label: NOAA Weather Radio named home warning system
detail: A White House policy names it the sole government-operated radio system for warnings into homes.

label: ARINC creates ACARS
detail: Text messaging between aircraft and airlines begins, to automate routine pilot-to-airline messages.

label: First Navstar GPS satellites
detail: Four Navstar satellites launched, the start of GPS.

label: Earliest recording of UVB-76
detail: The earliest preserved recording of "the Buzzer" on 4625 kHz dates from 1982.

label: First US commercial cellular service
detail: Ameritech opened service in Chicago; phones cost $2,200-$3,500.

label: FCC opens 2.4 GHz to unlicensed use
detail: An FCC ruling opens the 2.4 GHz ISM band to unlicensed spread-spectrum radios.

label: First GPS-timed grid sensor
detail: The first prototype phasor measurement unit used a GPS clock.

label: Project 25 established
detail: APCO, NASTD, NCS, NTIA and NSA launch the P25 digital radio standard effort.

label: Congress authorizes spectrum auctions
detail: The Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act of 1993 gives the FCC auction authority.

label: Cellular-capable scanners barred
detail: Scanners able to receive cellular frequencies may no longer be made or imported for US use.

label: First FCC spectrum auction
detail: Ten nationwide narrowband PCS licenses sell for about $617 million in five days.

label: GLONASS completed
detail: Russia's 24-satellite constellation, planned for 1987, was completed.

label: FCC adopts RF exposure limits
detail: The FCC adopts NCRP-based limits covering 300 kHz to 100 GHz; device SAR limits take effect Aug. 7.

label: First E-ZPass system
detail: The first E-ZPass electronic toll system goes live.

label: BARR aircraft-blocking program begins
detail: The forerunner of LADD lets owners keep aircraft off public flight-tracking displays.

label: First 802.11 standard
detail: The first IEEE 802.11 wireless LAN standard, up to 2 Mbit/s.

label: Bluetooth SIG formed
detail: Ericsson, Nokia, IBM, Toshiba and Intel form the Bluetooth Special Interest Group.

label: All FCC licensees must comply
detail: Deadline for all FCC licensees to comply with the RF exposure limits.

label: SOLAS AIS required on new ships
detail: Ships built on or after July 1, 2002 must carry AIS; existing ships phased in 2003-2008.

label: FCC approves HD Radio
detail: IBOC chosen as the US digital radio method after a 1998 petition.

label: MBTA tunnel cellular deal
detail: The MBTA signs a 15-year contract with InSite Wireless; Verizon service begins downtown in 2007.

label: MBTA signs subway cellular contract
detail: 15-year deal with InSite Wireless to wire tunnels for cell service.

label: UK Wireless Telegraphy Act 2006
detail: Section 48 makes intercepting messages not meant for you an offence in the UK.

label: Logan Runway 14/32 opens
detail: A one-way runway used only in strong northwest wind.

label: CharlieCard launches
detail: The MBTA introduces the CharlieCard, replacing the token.

label: TPMS mandate
detail: Tire pressure monitoring becomes required on 2008 model-year US vehicles built after Aug 31, 2007.

label: MBTA v. Anderson
detail: A court lets an MIT students' DEF CON 16 talk on the MBTA fare system proceed.

label: Mics barred from 700 MHz
detail: FCC 10-16 bars wireless mics from 698-806 MHz.

label: GPS 'Expandable 24'
detail: GPS becomes effectively a 27-slot constellation.

label: IARC classifies RF as Group 2B
detail: A 31-scientist IARC working group in Lyon classifies RF fields as possibly carcinogenic to humans.

label: First nationwide EAS test
detail: A roughly 30-second national Emergency Alert System test runs at 2 p.m. Eastern.

label: MassDOT Bluetooth travel times
detail: MassDOT first installs roadside Bluetooth readers for highway travel-time signs; Fast Lane is rebranded E-ZPass the same year.

label: Super Bowl XLVI wireless
detail: In Indianapolis, PWS manages 110 frequencies among several hundred in use.

label: FirstNet created
detail: The Middle Class Tax Relief and Job Creation Act creates FirstNet as an independent authority within NTIA.

label: T-Mobile reaches Green and Blue Lines
detail: Coverage extends to the Green Line (Park to Kenmore) and the Blue Line under the harbor.

label: Wireless Emergency Alerts launch
detail: Phones begin receiving geographically targeted emergency alerts.

label: Jammer disrupts Newark GBAS
detail: FAA complains after a truck-borne GPS jammer interferes with a landing-aid test at Newark Liberty.

label: RNAV departures begin at Logan
detail: Cambridge Day dates it to June 2013; the City of Cambridge says 2014. The FAA's Environmental Assessment came out in May 2013.

label: FCC proposes $31,875 fine
detail: FCC 13-106 released in the Newark jammer case.

label: Part 74 eligibility widened
detail: FCC 14-62 adds large venues and professional sound companies to wireless mic license eligibility.

label: CPDLC required on new aircraft in Europe
detail: The Single European Sky rule names VDL Mode 2 as the primary link.

label: AWS-3 auction raises $44.9 billion
detail: The AWS-3 auction sets a record that stands until the C-band auction.

label: ADS-B Exchange founded
detail: Started as a hobby project offering an unfiltered view of air traffic.

label: US AIS expansion deadline
detail: Previously exempt vessels covered by 33 CFR 164.46 must have AIS installed.

label: Galileo Initial Services
detail: European Commission declares Galileo's initial services available.

label: Super Bowl LI: about 1,000 frequencies
detail: About 1,000 frequencies in use in Houston; Karl Voss is the NFL lead coordinator.

label: TV incentive auction bidding closes
detail: $19.8 billion gross; $10.05 billion paid to 175 stations.

label: AT&T wins FirstNet contract
detail: FirstNet awards AT&T a 25-year contract to build and run the network.

label: Incentive auction ends
detail: The FCC broadcast incentive auction ends, starting the 39-month 600 MHz transition.

label: Wi-Fi 4, 5, 6 names
detail: The Wi-Fi Alliance adopts generation numbers for Wi-Fi standards.

label: Needham's Cabot Street candelabra rebuild completed
detail: New top UHF antenna and large low-band VHF antenna for WGBH.

label: FAA announces PIA; BARR renamed LADD
detail: New privacy measures for aircraft owners.

label: BeiDou goes global
detail: China's BDS-3 completes global coverage.

label: US ADS-B Out mandate takes effect
detail: Required in Class A, B and C and other designated airspace under 14 CFR 91.225.

label: ICNIRP 2020 guidelines
detail: ICNIRP publishes RF guidelines for 100 kHz-300 GHz, replacing its 1998 guidelines and covering 5G.

label: FCC opens 6 GHz
detail: The FCC makes 1,200 MHz at 5.925-7.125 GHz available for unlicensed use.

label: FCC opens 6 GHz to Wi-Fi
detail: 1,200 MHz at 5.925-7.125 GHz opened for unlicensed use, with AFC for standard-power access points.

label: Mics out of 600 MHz
detail: Wireless mics must stop operating on 617-652 and 663-698 MHz in the US.

label: TV repack deadline for last holdouts
detail: 987 full-power stations repacked or extended; cost about $2.75 billion.

label: FlightAware reports 30,000 receivers
detail: In 193 countries on all seven continents.

label: EU/UK transponder compliance date
detail: Current text of Reg 1207/2011 Art 5; OPSGROUP had reported June 7, 2020.

label: T-Band auction repealed
detail: The Don't Break Up the T-Band Act cancels the auction of public safety T-Band spectrum.

label: Curved approach to Logan 33L
detail: A Runway 33L RNP approach with curved segments is introduced to move noise away from homes.

label: Colorado media access rule
detail: HB 21-1250 requires fully encrypted agencies to adopt media access policies.

label: C-band auction ends at $80.9 billion
detail: Highest-grossing US spectrum auction: 280 MHz at 3.7-3.98 GHz.

label: C-band auction bidding closes
detail: Auction 107 clock phase closes at over $80.9 billion gross for 280 MHz at 3.7-3.98 GHz.

label: Ofcom 5G auction final results
detail: 700 MHz and 3.6-3.8 GHz sold for £1.379 billion to four UK operators.

label: FAA airworthiness directive on 5G and altimeters
detail: FAA found C-band 5G could stop some radio altimeters working properly.

label: AT&T shuts down 3G
detail: About 2.7 million customers affected; T-Mobile and Verizon followed by Jan 2023.

label: EASA GNSS interference bulletin
detail: EASA issues SIB 2022-02 on GNSS outages and alterations.

label: Matter 1.0
detail: The Connectivity Standards Alliance launches Matter 1.0 and its certification program.

label: Starlink Gen2 authorized
detail: FCC authorizes 7,500 Gen2 Starlink satellites in Ku and Ka bands.

label: MBTA picks L3Harris for P25
detail: A five-year, $93 million contract to replace EDACS with P25.

label: FCC auction authority lapses
detail: Congress lets the authority expire for the first time since 1993.

label: UK Emergency Alerts national test
detail: Phones across the UK sound a test alert at 3 p.m.

label: EU/UK retrofit deadline
detail: Last date for operators with a retrofit programme in place before December 7, 2020.

label: Ofcom updates UK amateur licences
detail: Ofcom sets 25 W, 100 W and 1000 W PEP tiers and new M8/M9 Intermediate call signs.

label: Wi-Fi CERTIFIED 7
detail: Wi-Fi 7 certification launches, with 320 MHz channels in the 6 GHz band.

label: FAA SAFO 24002
detail: FAA alerts operators to increasing GPS/GNSS disruptions.

label: FAA altimeter deadline for US airliners
detail: Part 121 aircraft must have approved, 5G-tolerant radio altimeters.

label: MBTA tap to ride
detail: Contactless bank cards and phone wallets start working at MBTA fare gates.

label: WHO-commissioned review on phones and cancer
detail: ARPANSA publicizes the Karipidis review: moderate-certainty evidence that mobile phones likely do not raise brain tumor risk.

label: Eversource smart meter rollout begins
detail: Itron smart meters start replacing Massachusetts electric meters in summer 2025.

label: Flightradar24 passes 50,000 ground stations
detail: About 7,000 are FR24-supplied kits; the rest are user-built.

label: GOES-19 becomes GOES East
detail: GOES-19 replaces GOES-16 at 75.2 degrees west.

label: NOAA-18 decommissioned
detail: First of the last three APT satellites shut down; NOAA-15 and -19 scheduled for August 2025.

label: Auction authority restored
detail: Public Law 119-21 restores FCC auction authority through 30 September 2034 and sets a spectrum pipeline.

label: Boston Police encrypt radio
detail: BPD switches to a digital encrypted system, with a delayed public feed.

label: Boston Police radio outage
detail: A BPD channel fails during a night of shootings, weeks after the new system was adopted; accounts of its length differ.

label: FCC proposes ending mandatory ATSC 1.0 simulcast
detail: Fifth Further Notice in GN Docket 16-142, adopted unanimously.

label: Starlink Gen2 doubled
detail: FCC authorizes 7,500 more Gen2 satellites, 15,000 total, including direct-to-cell.

label: Ofcom upper 6 GHz Wi-Fi
detail: Ofcom decides to allow AFC-controlled higher-power Wi-Fi across 6425-7125 MHz.

label: EASA SIB 2022-02 Revision 4
detail: Adds pilot-controller phraseology for GNSS interference.

label: WRC-27 opens in Shanghai
detail: The World Radiocommunication Conference runs 18 October - 12 November 2027.
